next_track.description: Skip to the next playlist item.

play.description: Resume/begin playback on the addressed player.

methods.notes: A control client discovers the Lyrion server (HTTP port 9000), then calls the CLI/JSON-RPC `players` query to enumerate connected players by MAC. Players themselves are found by the server via the UDP 3483 discovery exchange documented in protocol_details.slimproto_protocol below.

discovery.notes: A player's Wi-Fi/Ethernet MAC is its stable identity, carried in the SlimProto HELO and used as the addressing token in every CLI/JSON-RPC command. Do not key on IP: players are DHCP clients.

device.manufacturer: Slim Devices / Logitech (server now community-run as Lyrion)
device.name: Logitech Squeezebox (SlimProto player family)
device.notes:
Squeezebox is Slim Devices' (later Logitech's) family of network music players — Squeezebox 1/2/3/Classic, Boom, Transporter, Receiver, Radio and Touch. Logitech discontinued the whole hardware line in 2012 and later shut the mysqueezebox.com cloud, but the server software was handed to the community and continues as the Lyrion Music Server (v9.0, Nov 2024), GPL. A Squeezebox therefore never needed the vendor cloud for local playback: a player connects to a Lyrion server on the LAN and streams from it. This is a textbook rescue — the hardware keeps working as long as a server runs.
TWO PROTOCOLS live here:
  1. SlimProto (TCP 3483) — the player<->server control channel. The player
     connects out to the server; the server pushes `strm`/`audg`/`grfe`
     packets and the player answers with `HELO`/`STAT`/`BYE!`. Audio itself
     is pulled by the player over HTTP from the server (default port 9000).
  2. The server control API — a line CLI on TCP 9090 and the equivalent
     JSON-RPC over HTTP on port 9000 (POST /jsonrpc.js). This is what a
     third-party app uses to drive playback ("play", "pause", volume,
     playlist) by addressing a player by its MAC.
Controlling a Squeezebox means talking to its SERVER's control API; the server in turn speaks SlimProto to the player. Both are documented below.
DISCOVERY: a player looking for a server broadcasts a discovery datagram on UDP 3483; the server replies unicast to UDP 3483 on the player, which then opens the TCP 3483 control connection. A control client instead finds the server (its HTTP port 9000) and enumerates players through the CLI/JSON-RPC.

openness.notes: The protocol is published by the (originally vendor-run, now community) project and third-party clients are the point. Nothing here was reverse engineered; this file normalises the published protocol into the registry shape. Pin behaviour to the running server version, not to this document.

credentials.notes: The Wi-Fi passphrase is entered on the device, not carried over a link this spec documents. The control API (CLI/JSON-RPC) can be protected by HTTP Basic auth / a CLI `login` command when the server is configured for it; by default it is open on the LAN.
stored_on_device: Wi-Fi credentials (entered on the player's own UI)

factory_reset.effect: Per-model reset procedures exist (front-panel key combos on the Classic/Boom/Radio/Touch) but are not transcribed here. A reset returns the player to first-boot network setup; it stores no cloud credential once pointed at a local server.

methods.description: Use the player's front-panel/on-screen setup to join Wi-Fi (or plug in Ethernet) and point it at a Lyrion server's IP. The player then opens the SlimProto TCP 3483 connection on its own.

steps.action: On the player, run its setup and join the home network (or connect Ethernet).
Point the player at the Lyrion server address (or let UDP 3483 discovery find it).
steps.expect: The player connects to the server and appears in its player list.

setup.notes: A player is provisioned through its own on-device UI (or wired Ethernet): it is told the Wi-Fi network and the address of a Lyrion server, then connects out on TCP 3483. No cloud account is required for a local server. The provisioning UI is not documented here — mark low.

rejoin.notes: A player can be re-pointed at a different server from its own settings UI, and the server can move a player with the SlimProto `serv` command. No factory reset is needed to change servers or networks in place.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. Every fact below is transcribed from the Lyrion (ex-Logitech Media Server) project documentation and the community SlimProto wiki. The server is GPL and is the authoritative implementation — verify against it, not this file.

http_endpoints.description: The server's JSON-RPC control endpoint on HTTP port 9000. Body is {"id":1,"method":"slim.request","params":["<player-mac>",[<command>...]]}. Anything the line CLI (TCP 9090) can do is available here, addressed to a player by its MAC. Commands are URL-percent-escaped UTF-8 tokens, e.g. ["mixer","volume","50"] or ["playlist","index","+1"]. A bare "" player id targets the server itself (e.g. the "players" query to enumerate players).
http_endpoints.name: Lyrion JSON-RPC control

fields.description: [player-id, [command tokens]] — player-id is the MAC, or "" for a server-scoped query.
fields.name: params

client_messages.HELO: Player registration: a DeviceID byte ('2'=Squeezebox, '4'=Squeezebox2, '5'=Transporter, '10'=Boom), firmware revision, 6-byte MAC, a 16-byte UUID on newer firmware, WLAN channel bitfield, a bytes-received counter, and an optional comma-separated capability string (codecs wma/flc/pcm/ aac/mp3/ogg in preference order, plus MaxSampleRate, Model, HasDigitalOut, SyncgroupID).
client_messages.IR: Raw infrared remote codes from the player's remote.
client_messages.STAT: Heartbeat / event: status codes such as STMc (connected), STMd (decoder ready), STMu (underrun), STMn (unsupported format), plus buffer fullness, elapsed time and Wi-Fi signal.

discovery.description: A player broadcasts a discovery datagram on UDP 3483; the server answers unicast to UDP 3483 on the player, which then opens the TCP 3483 control connection. (The exact discovery datagram byte layout is not restated here — the port and direction are the load-bearing facts.)

framing.server_to_client: 2-byte length (network byte order, excludes itself) + 4-byte command tag + data.

server_messages.aude: Enable/disable the SPDIF and DAC outputs.
server_messages.audg: Volume: 16.16 fixed-point left/right gains plus preamp.
server_messages.grfe: Display bitmap (e.g. 320x32 on Squeezebox3), optional LZF compression.
server_messages.serv: Switch the player to another server (IP + optional SyncgroupID).
server_messages.strm: Stream control (24+ bytes). Subcommand: 's' start, 'p' pause, 'u' unpause, 'q' stop, 't' status, 'f' flush, 'a' skip. Carries a format byte ('p' PCM, 'm' MP3, 'f' FLAC, 'w' WMA, 'a' AAC), sample size/rate/channels/endianness, a buffer threshold, a 16.16 fixed-point replay-gain, the server IP+port, and then a literal embedded HTTP request (e.g. `GET /stream.mp3?player=<mac> HTTP/1.0`) that the player issues to fetch the audio (with a Basic-auth header if the server is password-protected).

slimproto_protocol.transport: TCP, server listens on 3483; player connects out
